name: Menlo Park Police Cadet Program (Explorer Post 844)
what_you_do: Cadets do ride-alongs with patrol officers, sit with 9-1-1 dispatchers and detectives, and help at parades, traffic control and community events. They train in first aid, CPR, search and rescue and more.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. You can start applying at 13 and a half. You must keep a 2.0 GPA, pass a background check and pass an oral board interview. The page does not list a residency rule.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. A 2019 participation form on the page lists a $55 academy fee and a uniform that costs about $150 to $200. The current page does not list costs, so confirm them.
duration: Ongoing. Volunteer at least 10 hours a month. The page says it is meant to be a long-term commitment, and cadets age out at 21.
deadline_text: No deadline or application window is posted. Apply any time.
how_to_apply: Fill out the cadet application and the participation agreement from the page, then mail them to Attn: Police Cadet Program, 701 Laurel St., Menlo Park, CA 94025. Questions: Police Corporal Galen Fliege, gpfliege@menlopark.gov, 650-330-6300.
notes: You must finish the Peninsula Law Enforcement Cadet Academy. The 2019 participation form describes it as eight Sundays at College of San Mateo plus one Saturday at Huddart Park, with tests you must pass at 70 percent, and says you need your own ride. It also lists one evening meeting a month. The page is now called Police Cadets, but the forms still say Police Explorer Post 844. The application asks for a Social Security number and driver license number for the background check, and a parent must sign if you are under 18. The page lists no meeting schedule or dates.
